Title: Benchmark mature Manhattan's market reach against the adopted floor tiers
Description:
Owner question: what does the free market actually dictate in developed, zero-gap Manhattan (West Village, East Village and the like)? Measured over the 27,302 Manhattan addresses (768,847 units, 80.2% of the borough) with 0/15 gaps under reach_tiers.yaml; full table in docs/market_reach_manhattan.md.

Every category's unit-weighted p80 nearest distance sits far INSIDE the adopted reach: restaurant 80 m vs 400 (0.20), grocery 156 vs 800 (0.20), pharmacy 216 vs 800 (0.27), fitness 167 vs 1,200 (0.14), clinic 223 vs 960 (0.23), hardware 334 vs 960 (0.35), tailor 449 vs 960 (0.47), convenience 223 vs 400 (0.56), laundry 188 vs 320 (0.59). Not an artifact of the completeness filter (over ALL Manhattan addresses every category is still 16–74% of the adopted tier), not dominated by a few NTAs (top 10 = 49% of complete units, 36 of ~40 NTAs), no lot-size bias.

Consequences the artifact must carry: (1) under the adopted tiers Manhattan almost never gaps, so the screen's discriminating power lives in the outer boroughs — the D41 tiers are a FLOOR ('nobody should be beyond this'), not the market standard. (2) 'What the market dictates' is density-dependent: Manhattan's distances are short because its density is 19–30k units/km², and adopting them citywide would flag most of Queens. (3) The right refinement is therefore density-class reach — reach(c) per density class from complete areas within that class, so a gap means 'short of what places like this one actually have'. That is an owner modeling decision; the adopted D41 table stands until it is made.

Carry: complete-area p80s are supply-revealed and inherit D33's caveat (a citywide under-supplied category looks 'naturally' wide); pairing them with D41's cited floors bounds reach from both sides.

Title: ACS vehicle-ownership ingest (B08201 + B25044) and a renter_share MOE
Description:
The pre-test came first and came back NEGATIVE, which is why the ingest was not optional. Over MN+BK hexes with population ≥ 100 (n = 1,875), renter_share's partial Spearman with reach outcomes NET of population density is 0.13 (POI/km²), 0.07 (present_count), −0.07 (median nearest m) and −0.02 (max_ratio, p = 0.37); it adds under 2 points of R² over log density, and in Manhattan the sign flips. Renter_share proxies DENSITY (ρ = 0.62 citywide), not mode (ρ = 0.09 within Manhattan), and its ACS MOE (17% of estimate, hex median 0.072) leaves 30% of MN+BK hexes indeterminate at a 0.70 cut. So a car-dependence signal needs a real vehicle variable.

Built: `grid/acs.py::build_acs` now pulls B08201_001E/M and _002E/M → `zero_vehicle_hh_share[_moe]`; B25044_002/003/009/010 E/M → `zero_vehicle_owner_share[_moe]` and `zero_vehicle_renter_share[_moe]`; and B25003_001M/_003M → `renter_share_moe`, which the table had been missing. All cells verified against the 2023 ACS variables.json, plus a runtime cross-table check (B25044 owner+renter totals vs B25003 total, raising above a 2% aggregate discrepancy). Extensive quantities are apportioned tract→hex by PLUTO unit share exactly as population and households already were; MOEs use root-sum-of-squares for apportioned sums and then the ACS-handbook proportion formula (`_moe_proportion`, with the documented negative-subtraction fallback). Raw response cached at data/raw/acs/tracts_2023.json (one call per vintage); 7 new nullable columns via ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS; registry.yaml mirrors the variables. Rebuild: 5,978 hexes, row count unchanged. tests/test_acs.py 8 tests (6 new).

Headline: citywide median zero_vehicle_hh_share 0.321 (MOE 27.8% of estimate), MN+BK median 0.585 (MOE 14.2%, n = 1,960). Within MN+BK it correlates MORE with renter_share (0.712) than with population density (0.519), so whether it is a genuinely distinct mode signal is still open; no threshold or class was built on it.

CAVEAT the database cannot enforce: proportion MOEs on hexes with a near-zero apportioned housing-unit denominator can exceed 1 (one hex at households ≈ 1.8 shows renter_share_moe 5.3). Any consumer sorting or filtering on these MOE columns must also gate on a minimum apportioned denominator.

Title: In-building laundry as a supply input: LL84/LL133 hookups + StreetEasy advertised laundry
Description:
Laundry is the second-largest lead category in the address screen, and the owner ruling that opened E10 also ruled that in-building laundry (basement or in-unit) is a SUPPLY-side input: an address that has it does not experience a laundromat gap. This ticket is the two sources for it.

LL84/LL133 benchmarking laundry hookups → staging.ll84_laundry, analysis.address_laundry: 30,966 BBLs, which clears 710 of 43,726 MN+BK laundry leads = 1.6%. The reason it clears so little is itself the finding: 92% of laundry leads are in buildings under 6 units, and LL84's 25,000 sq ft reporting threshold never covers them. Implementation note that will bite anyone re-running it — Socrata TRANSPOSES the in-unit and common-area columns across vintages, so fields are resolved by display name, not by field id. Second source: advertised laundry scraped from StreetEasy listing pages via Tavily (registry `streeteasy_listings`, verified).

What this means for the model, and why it is not a filter: NYCHVS 2023 says 74% of 1-unit and 50% of 2-unit MN+BK dwellings have an in-unit washer, so for small buildings in-building laundry can only ever be a RATE, never a per-address fact — it belongs in the grade as a demand haircut, not as supply subtracted from a count. Anchoring laundromat supply itself (the DCWP adapter, whose ingest was empty) is the companion half and is tracked under E10.

Title: Address-grain demographics: `analysis.address_demographics` from each lot's own tract
Description:
URGENT because it is the missing carrier that made three days of work invisible: D49, D53 and D54 all landed on HEX tables the address screen never reads, so none of it reached anything the owner looks at. D38 made the residential address the unit; the demographics had not followed.

Method, chosen to be the least-modelled input possible: an address sits in exactly one tract, so the tract's ACS values and MOEs are taken AS-IS — no apportionment, no interpolation, no point-in-polygon join. Tract assignment is PLUTO's own `bct2020` field on the lot (the same field grid/acs.py already trusted for hex weights), so address → tract is a BBL lookup against the raw PLUTO extract; no TIGER download, and no new Census call (built from the existing raw ACS cache). Columns: tract GEOID, median_hh_income + moe (B19013), renter_share + moe (B25003, ACS-handbook proportion MOE via `_moe_proportion`), zero_vehicle_hh_share + moe (B08201), zero_vehicle_owner_share / zero_vehicle_renter_share + moe (B25044), population and households (B01003/B11001) for reference, acs_year.

Results: 767,337 rows, 767,331 with a tract (99.9992%; the 6 without get NULLs and are never dropped); 2,225 distinct tracts; ZERO tracts carry more than one distinct income value, which is the proof that this is a lookup and not an apportionment. Citywide median household income $91,389, MN+BK $83,083; median zero-vehicle share 31.2% citywide, 52.4% MN+BK; median income MOE 25.7% of estimate, and 53.0% of addresses sit within one MOE of the D49 threshold ($102,315) — the indeterminacy that retired the binary badge, reproduced at address grain.

CAVEAT the database cannot enforce: population and households are the tract's FULL count repeated on every address in it, so summing them across addresses is an N-times overcount; rates are safe per address or as medians. `analysis.hex_demographics` is frozen history from here on.

Implementation: src/loci/model/address_demographics.py, DDL in 002_schema.sql, `loci address-demographics [--dry-run]`; tests/test_address_demographics.py 6 tests.

Title: Move the Google validator's sampling frame to gap addresses (GTM-48 prerequisite)
Description:
URGENT and a hard prerequisite for GTM-48, because it is the check that decides whether ~$300 of Google budget buys anything. validation/sample.py still drew HEX CENTROIDS stratified by income decile from analysis.hex_demographics — points no lead refers to (a hex centroid can sit in a park, a rail yard or mid-block), validating a screen that no longer speaks in hexes (D38).

`draw_sample` now draws rows of analysis.address_gaps, restricted to MN+BK (D48) and to eligible lots, stratified income decile × missing-this-category. The income decile is NTILE(10) over analysis.address_demographics.median_hh_income — the tract's own ACS median on the lot's BBL (D56), no apportionment. The missing/present split is the whole point: measuring Google's enumeration only where loci says a category is MISSING cannot separate coverage bias from a real hole (D29, CONTEXT 7.1 prediction P3), so the PRESENT half of each stratum is the control. Both sides of every row are measured at the lot's own lon/lat at the D53 649 m radius, so the Google count and the local canonical count are like-for-like by construction. Address-weighted by default (one lot, one draw); `--unit-weighted` draws proportional to units_capped (Efraimidis–Spirakis, without replacement) for reading the sample as a statement about households behind a gap.

Schema: analysis.coverage_validation gains nullable address_id and borough; h3_index stays and is NULL on address rows. The hex-era PRIMARY KEY (h3_index, category) had to GO — a DuckDB PK column is implicitly NOT NULL and there is no ALTER TABLE DROP CONSTRAINT, so the table physically could not hold an address row; `sample.ensure_address_frame()` migrates an existing database (rename → re-apply 002_schema.sql → copy rows back by column name; guarded, no-op once migrated, never fires on --dry-run) and run() maintains uniqueness itself.

FRAMES MUST NEVER BE POOLED: the 2,970 rows written 2026-09-02/03 are the pre-D38 hex frame at the legacy 800 m disc (radius_m NULL) — different unit, different geometry, different radius. They stay for the D29 hardware/fitness/clinic split and are usable only against each other; every statistic must filter on one frame (h3_index IS NOT NULL or address_id IS NOT NULL).

Two facts GTM-48's budget request must carry, surfaced by the plan (20/stratum, 14 mapped categories, clinic skipped, 5,185 addresses over 265 strata = 5,277 calls at 649 m): grocery has ZERO missing addresses in the eligible MN+BK frame, so its 200 control calls buy no gap observations; and fitness/pharmacy/nails_beauty/hardware have income deciles with no missing address, so their missing arm is thinner than 10 strata. Also: plan()'s est_cost_usd assumes the 5,000 free calls are untouched, but 2,978 are already spent — the true incremental cost is nearer $170 than the printed $8.86. Budget off the ledger, not that number.

Code only; no Google call made, ledger still 2,978/3,000. CLI: `loci validate --per-stratum N --boroughs MN,BK [--unit-weighted] [--seed S] [--dry-run]`. Tests: tests/test_sample.py 16 (11 new).

Title: Supply-set re-run (principled), DCWP laundry anchor, alcohol overlay, E10 category plan
Description:
The D52 supply-set principle put into effect, plus the two source fixes it exposed. MN+BK re-run, under 5 minutes end to end.

Anchor coverage decides which categories the principle touches: it qualifies nails_beauty 3.04, bar 1.85, restaurant 1.46, convenience 1.43 (SNAP) and cafe_bakery 1.23 against ZBP; grocery 0.58 and hair_barber 0.39 are too thin, and eight categories have no anchor loaded at all. So PRINCIPLED dropped lone aggregator records ONLY in those five (restaurant 40,191→20,476, cafe 10,059→4,638, nails 9,810→4,308, bar 7,505→3,304, convenience 2,850→1,779; 36% overall) and the ten unanchored categories are bit-identical — which is the whole point of the principle over a global corroboration rule. Share of eligible addresses beyond reach rose only in those five (bar 25→39%, cafe 10→21%, convenience 9→15%, restaurant 3→5%); lead_category changed for 23% of eligible MN+BK addresses. The prior screen is kept as analysis.address_gaps_prev and data/interim/address_gaps_prev.parquet; provenance now records supply_set + supply_hash. A NULL-name crash in the booth-renter code was fixed.

Two caveats that must travel with the numbers: nails qualifies as anchored for the WRONG REASON — the DOS registry itself runs ~3× ZBP (residual booth renters, non-salon licences); and the webmap POI layer read poi_dedup.is_canonical directly, showing 100,213 known locations while gaps were measured against 64,303 (being fixed to read analysis.poi_supply and to draw excluded records distinctly).

Laundry anchor, and why the adapter had been silent: the DCWP LICENCE roster (w7w3-xahh) has no retail-laundry category at all — 6 'Laundries' licences, all expired 2023. Retail laundries exist only in DCWP INSPECTIONS (jzhd-m6uv, business_category 'Retail Laundry' and 'Dry Cleaners - 230'; industrial laundry excluded). The historical-licences file (m4ph-grrm) shows 2,587 CURRENT LAUNDRY rows but is a frozen October-2013 snapshot — recorded here so nobody takes the bait. Staged 2,277 MN+BK establishments (99.9% geocoded), 1,561 active; anchor_coverage 1,561/1,475 ZBP = 1.06, so laundry QUALIFIES. 1,015 are within 40 m of an existing canonical laundry, 546 are new. No staleness cut (inspections are enforcement-driven) and the feed starts 2023-07, so a never-inspected laundry is indistinguishable from a gap.

Alcohol overlay (D52(c)) shipped: every active SLA licence in MN+BK as a toggleable layer, symbol classes on_premises 10,757 / off_premises_liquor 863 / off_premises_beer 3,438 / other 451 / unclassified 617 (16,126 total), a drift test on the 55-value vocabulary, and verification that it touches neither the gap nor the POI layer. Liquor stays an overlay, never a 16th category.

Category expansion (D55) planned in the same pass and pushed as milestone E10: dentist (NPPES anchor verified, GTM-113), specialty_food (NYS Ag & Markets retail food stores 9a8c-vfzj, GTM-114), eye_care (NPPES covers only the clinical half, GTM-115), dollar_variety (no anchor, GTM-116), vet_pet (no bulk anchor exists, GTM-117), plus a mechanics ticket (TIER_WEIGHTS re-partition, MIN_PRESENT 12-of-15 re-derivation, max-ratio monotone in category count, GTM-112). Dropped with reasons: dry cleaners (already inside laundry, NAICS 812310+812320), shipping & mail (no anchor, and NAICS 491110 is government so ZBP can never check it), florist/books/phone repair (three unrelated codes, tiny counts), auto & gas (a drive-time trade area inside a pedestrian screen). Owner 2026-09-09: liquor stays a MAP OVERLAY and is dropped from E10 — D52(c) stands.

Listings: only StreetEasy unit pages expose amenities + address + past listings via Tavily (Zillow and RentHop render without amenities, Apartments.com refuses). Bay Ridge pilot: 222 listings / 52 BBLs, 173 in-building, 23 in-unit, 0 explicit none — silence is never absence — annotating 41 of 98 ≥6-unit laundry leads (2.2% of all Bay Ridge leads); address→BBL matched within 5 m from the page's own coordinates. Coverage is size-selected (median 38 units where found vs 14.5 where not) and archival (213/222 past listings). The owner-approved full MN+BK sweep (~34k calls, ~37k credits, ~$294, ≥6-unit addresses first, paced, parquet sink, one short merge) is tracked under GTM-125, not here.

Also queued behind the webmap fix, not part of this ticket: `loci ingest-dcwp --no-stage --apply && loci dedup` then score / address-gaps / export.

Title: ACS age/race/education/household-size at address grain + warehouse consolidation (34 → 26 objects, address long/wide split)
Description:
Owner asked for age, race/ethnicity, education and household size. grid/acs.py now pulls 118 E+M variables (every cell verified against the live 2023 variables.json; fetched in 3 chunks of ≤48 because the Census API caps a request at 50): median age (B01002); under-18, 18–34 and 65+ shares from B01001 summed across sexes, with 35–64 deliberately left as the residual so a fourth column cannot read as independent; white, Black and Asian non-Hispanic and Hispanic-any-race shares (B03002); bachelor's-or-higher share of 25+ (B15003); average household size (B25010) and one-person-household share (B11016). MOEs travel with every field: RSS for apportioned and multi-cell sums, the handbook proportion formula for shares, the incumbent weighted mean for the two intensive fields. A B01001-vs-B01003 per-tract population cross-check (>2% aggregate raises) joins the D54 B25044/B25003 one. Population-weighted hex figures against known NYC values: white NH 31.4% (~31), Black NH 20.7% (~22), Asian NH 14.6% (~15), Hispanic 28.5% (~29), college 39.7% (~40). Why the decision matters: these landed first on hex_demographics and were then COPIED onto address_gaps by containing hex — doubly modelled (tract→hex by unit share, hex→address by containment) and a step function at hex edges — while a parallel session built D56's tract-direct analysis.address_demographics the same day. Two tables answered one question. Ruling: the tract-direct table is canonical because a lot sits in exactly one tract and there is nothing to apportion; it was extended to the same 20 columns by IMPORTING acs.py's cell lists and helpers, the 36 hex-copied columns were stripped from the gap table, and a drift test fails if any hex demographic lacks an address twin. Unit-weighted citywide from the canonical table: white NH 35.0%, Black NH 19.1%, Asian NH 14.4%, Hispanic 26.7%, college 44.6%, median age 39.0, avg household 2.47 (units, not people, are the weight, so these differ from the hex figures by construction). Also caught: `loci address-demographics` had never been re-run after the extension landed, so every new column was NULL on all 767,337 rows until this session. Title: Residential development pipeline: DCP Housing Database + DOB CO at job grain, pipeline exposure on analysis.address, webmap overlay
Description:
Owner asked (2026-09-09) to build the pipeline layer with DOB permits and CO dates, to answer the density-shock question (QUESTIONS T7): which gap addresses are about to gain residents? DCP Housing Database (br6q-ssj3, v25Q4, data through 2026-01-21): 109,076 jobs with unique job_number, 100% geocoded with BBL/BIN on MN+BK. Completion status derived from DOB CO feeds (bs8b-p36w BIS, pkdm-hqz6 DOB NOW, both refreshing daily). Trap: 436 MN+BK jobs (11,407 units) are still marked Permitted in DCP but hold a CO issued after the cutoff; joined on job_number to override DCP status stale. Data problems: pkdm-hqz6 CO date is text (MM/DD/YY h:mm:ss AM), bs8b-p36w contains a literal 2105-11-05 (both handled in the adapter). One new table analysis.dev_pipeline (one row per DOB job, 48,762 MN+BK jobs at job grain), 12 measures extended analysis.address by UPDATE only (units_permitted_400m, units_completed_24mo_400m / _60mo_400m, nearest_large_project_id / _units / _stage / _date, pipeline_asof): reusing score/access network-distance helpers, NOT address_category (because exposure is category-independent). Webmap: Development pipeline overlay (net_units ≥50, stages permitted / partial-CO / complete ≤60-mo; filed and withdrawn never drawn): 589 jobs (MN 210, BK 379; 108,528 homes), sized by band 50–99/100–299/300+, coloured by stage, hollow ring = temporary CO; gap popups carry the exposure; min-units-permitted selector filters the gap layer. Data dir 42 → 50.6 MB; nearest project dictionary-encoded per file. Suite 333 → 364. Caveats: (1) DCP vintage lag (forward pipeline is a floor); (2) TCO ≠ finished building (co_type filters); (3) zombie permits (1,348 jobs / 9,468 units, 23% of permitted, >5yr old never completed); (4) withdrawn-after-permit kept, excluded from measures; (5) negative net_units (demolitions) ingested, measures count ≥1; (6) never ratio units_complete and net_units; (7) 24mo ⊂ 60mo, never add; (8) job ≠ masterplan; (9) no under_construction stage, deliberately. Bug fixed: db.init_schema() builds address_gaps view after 002, ALTERs at tail of 002. Live run: 281,842 addresses annotated in 2m45s; non-filtering proof exact. Investor review (same day, QUESTIONS T7) found rooftops→retail lag is rational landlord optionality, not friction — pipeline is a timing annotation only. `loci ingest-dcp-housing`, `loci pipeline`, `loci export-webmap` all --dry-run. Registry drift fixed: lodes_wac temporal line corrected (loaded vintages are 2002/2013/2023, not annual series).
